title: fix(runtime)!: the /mcp bridge reads objects from the protocol's merged view, so a package's objects are listed, described and gated
body:
Fixes #25120

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

The `/mcp` HTTP bridge now reads objects from the protocol's merged view, the read REST serves. `list_objects` and `describe_object` see every object `GET /api/v1/meta/object` lists to the same caller, and the API-exposure gate the data verbs ask refuses a package object declared `apiEnabled: false`. Nothing is copied into the `metadata` service: a second copy would be a second thing to keep in sync.

## The defect, measured on base `4e2c42f363`

`buildMcpBridge` answered `list_objects` and `describe_object` from the `metadata` service (`listObjects()` / `getObject()`). The exposure gate every runtime data door asks (`refuseUnexposedDataAction` in `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, called by `callData`) read the same service and treated a missing copy as "no declaration", that is, allowed. That service holds a copy of an object only where something put one there. On a kernel with an `environmentId`, the full boot bridge is off. That covers `createStandaloneStack` (`os dev` as `env_local`, `os serve`, `os start`) and the cloud single-environment runtime. So an object that a package or a plugin registers in the `SchemaRegistry` during the boot gets no copy.

Real kernels (`ObjectKernel` + `MetadataPlugin` + `ObjectQLPlugin` over better-sqlite3 `:memory:`). The `environmentId` shape uses `createStandaloneStack`'s plugin options verbatim. The fixture package has two objects, one declared `apiEnabled: false`, registered through the kernel's `manifest` service:

| shape, when the package registered | `metadata.getObject` | REST lists | bridge lists | describe | gated `query` | gated `create` |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `env_local`, during the boot | absent | 2 | **0** | **null** | **served** | **reached the driver** |
| `env_local`, installed after the boot (`source: 'marketplace'`) | copied | 2 | 2 | served | 404 | 404 |
| no `environmentId`, during the boot | copied | 2 | 2 | served | 404 | 404 |
| no `environmentId`, installed after the boot | copied | 2 | 2 | served | 404 | 404 |

The first row is the card's live reading in miniature: a short list presented as a complete `totalCount`, "not found" for every package object, and `query_records` served. The other three rows are controls: the boot bridge and the late-manifest bridge already copy, so they were right and must stay right.

**The gate half is real.** The same object declared `apiEnabled: false` was served by `query_records`, and `create_record` got past the gate to the driver. The runtime dispatcher's `/data` door shares the gate, and on that shape it answered `GET /data/qa_pkg_gated` with 200 and `POST` reached the driver. `RestServer` refused the same object, because its gate already reads the protocol's by-name read.

**The multi-tenant (`environmentId` kernel) path.** The merged read is per environment there. The bridge resolves `protocol` through `deps.resolveService(context, 'protocol', envId)`, the same scoped seam `metadata` and the skill read use. Each environment kernel's `getMetaItems` reads its own `ObjectQL` registry (`readFlattenedMetaItems`: "the SchemaRegistry is owned by THIS kernel's ObjectQL instance"). Measured: two `environmentId` kernels behind one host each list and gate their own package and none of the other's. That run is red with the fix ablated, because both lists come back empty.

**The stdio half measures the same defect.** That transport is held off by the dispatch, so this is reported and not widened. Same fixture, `env_local`, during the boot, driven through the real `MCPServerPlugin` stdio session: `list_objects` gave `{"objects": [], "totalCount": 0}`, `describe_object` gave `Object "qa_pkg_open" not found`, and `query_records` on the `apiEnabled: false` object was served (`total: 0`). The control without an `environmentId` lists, describes and refuses `OBJECT_API_DISABLED`.

## What changed

- **`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`.** `list_objects` / `listObjectsDiagnosed` and `describe_object` read `getMetaItems({ type: 'object' })` through the existing `McpMergedMetadataRead` seam. This is the shape commit e783e163d gave the skill read. The unwrap moved into one helper (`readMergedItems`) shared by the skill read and the object reads, and the skill read's behaviour is unchanged. `describe_object` answers from the same listing, so every listed object can be described. The three outcomes are the skill read's. With no merged read on the host, the code reads the `metadata` service as before. When the merged read answers, it is served. When the merged read throws, the error goes to the client and nothing falls back. `listObjectsDiagnosed` keeps asking `listDiagnosed('object')` for the `partial` verdict.
- **`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`.** The exposure gate reads the object by name through the protocol, the read `RestServer`'s own gate makes (`enforceApiAccess`). It uses the execution face (`getMetaItemForExecution`) where the protocol has one, and `getMetaItem` otherwise. A refusal `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` reads as "no declaration", as `RestServer` reads it, and the data plane then refuses with that code. A host whose protocol has no by-name read keeps reading the `metadata` service. A merged read that throws falls back to the `metadata` service's copy, the source this gate read before. An outage must not widen exposure, and the caller's existing fail-open `catch` is unchanged.
- **`packages/runtime/src/domains/data-write-request-gate.test.ts`, a fixture re-judged.** Its dispatcher door used to model the gate's old source (a `metadata` fake answered from the registry). The rig's protocol cannot read without a metadata store, so with this change that door passed only through the outage fallback. The registry-backed by-name stub now lives in `bootStore` (`stubObjectReads`) and serves both doors, and the dispatcher door is given no `metadata` service. A gate that stopped reading the protocol now reds 12 of its rows (measured below). 73 of 73 rows are green with the fix.
- **`.changeset/25120-mcp-package-objects.md`.** A `patch` for `@objectstack/runtime`, with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Both declaration lines are in the body.

## Contract

Every input whose answer changes, old to new:

1. **`list_objects` (`POST /api/v1/mcp`) on a kernel with an `environmentId`, for an object a package or plugin registered during the boot.** Old: omitted, with `totalCount` short and no `partial`. New: listed. The non-`sys_` set equals what `GET /api/v1/meta/object` serves the same caller.
2. **`describe_object` and `validate_expression` on such an object.** Old: `Object "NAME" not found`. New: described (fields, label, `enableFeatures`).
3. **`query_records`, `get_record`, `aggregate_records`, `create_record`, `update_record`, `delete_record` on such an object declared `enable.apiEnabled: false`.** Old: served, and the writes reached the store. New: `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED`, and the store is never asked. With an `apiMethods` whitelist, a verb it leaves out gets `405 OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` with `allowed`.
4. **The same declaration on every other door that asks this gate** (the runtime dispatcher's `/data` door, the `@objectstack/hono` catch-all; `callData` under business actions and declarative endpoints). Old: served. New: the same refusals as item 3, the codes `RestServer` answers.
5. **A disabled package's objects, where the `metadata` service still holds a copy.** For example, a kernel without an `environmentId`. Old: `list_objects` listed them and `describe_object` described them, while REST listed neither. New: omitted and not found, as REST answers.
6. **A data verb on a disabled package's object declared `apiEnabled: false`.** Old: `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED`. New: `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, the code `RestServer` answers. The status does not move.
7. **An object whose served definition differs from the `metadata` service's copy** (for example, a stored environment row layered over it). Old: MCP discovery and the gate read the copy. New: they read the definition REST serves.
8. **`list_objects` / `describe_object` while the metadata store cannot be read.** Old: the `metadata` service's listing. New: the protocol's `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` error envelope, which is what `GET /api/v1/meta/object` answers and what the skill prompt read already answers.

Unchanged: objects that already had a copy are listed and gated as before. That covers every object on a kernel without an `environmentId`, a marketplace install on any kernel, and a runtime-authored object. A host with no merged read keeps reading the `metadata` service. The gate's outage branch judges the copy, as before. `packages/mcp` is untouched.

## Pins

`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-object-discovery.test.ts`, 41 cases. The pins read the bridge the real `/mcp` entry (`HttpDispatcher.handleMcp`) hands the MCP service, so `list_objects` renders `totalCount` from `listObjectsDiagnosed().objects`:

- For each of the four rows above: `list_objects` lists the package's objects, its non-`sys_` set equals `GET /meta/object`'s for the same caller, and it is not `partial`. `describe_object` answers both objects, including `apiEnabled: false`. Each of the six data verbs refuses the gated object with `{ code: 'OBJECT_API_DISABLED', status: 404 }`, and no protocol data method or engine `aggregate` is called. Control: `query_records` serves the exposed object.
- A disabled package's objects are neither listed nor described, with the precondition that the copy still exists.
- Two environments behind one host each list, describe and gate their own package and not the other's.

**Red before, green after.** Each leg's direction was predicted before running. Mutations were landed and restored by `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, blob changed; restored blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty). The whole-file leg was restored with `git checkout HEAD`, with blob equality and an empty `git diff HEAD` checked.

| leg | mutation | result |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| main | both source files at base `4e2c42f363` (blobs `5d19bd3b7a`, `616639b765`) | 13 failed, 28 passed: `env_local` during-boot list, describe and six verbs; the disabled-package pin; four two-environment pins |
| discovery | `readMergedObjects` answers `undefined` (the `metadata` service read) | 5 failed, 36 passed |
| gate | `readExposureDeclaration` always reads the copy | 8 failed, 33 passed |
| rig | the gate leg, against `data-write-request-gate.test.ts` | 12 failed, 61 passed (the dispatcher door's exposure rows) |
| fix | HEAD | 41 passed; rig 73 passed |

## Local verification, on `d19b65bf1c` (the final commit, `origin/main` `1b3b65e643` merged in)

- `@objectstack/runtime` unit layer (`--project local`), every file in three chunks: 433 files; 6835 passed, 19 skipped, 0 failed (147 + 141 + 145 files). `test:repo` is CI's: the diff touches none of its three files and the derivation does not name it.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit`, plus `check:test-typecheck` OK; both new or edited test files are in the `tsconfig.test.json` program).
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 68 commands, all exit 0. The 10 families declared WIDE-population, all exit 0: `check:init-service-contract`, `check:live-db-isolation`, `check:meta-type-normalized`, `check:optional-error-sink`, `check:resume-authority-declared`, `check:runner-env-posture`, `check:settings-bind-window`, `check:startup-registry-verdict`, `check:verify-stand-in`, `check:wildcard-fallthrough`. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was measured after a full workspace build. An earlier run on a partial build said PREREQUISITE NOT MET, and that is not counted.
- `--ran` reconciliation, each line carrying its captured exit code: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 68 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 68 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).`
- `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`): exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main --event PAYLOAD`, with PAYLOAD a `pull_request` event carrying this body: exit 0. `✓ This diff introduces no `major` bump.` and `✓ LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② `no (narrowing)` and metadata-protocol `none`, and it introduces no changeset entry graded `minor` or above and moves no metadata-protocol baseline`.
- `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base 1b3b65e643` (the merge base): exit 0. `✓ check-adr-0087-registration: 1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition.` (`[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing]  not-required (no-migration-prescription)`).

The CI families (Lint and Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core) are CI's to report on this PR. Dogfood and the live-PG/MySQL temporal job do not run on a PR.

## Acceptance notes

- **Card acceptance item 3 (walked on a cloud environment with a marketplace app installed): NOT MEASURED.** The cloud host lives in `objectstack-ai/cloud`, outside this session. In this repo the shape is the `environmentId` kernel, pinned above with `createStandaloneStack`'s options. On that shape, a package registered during the boot is the one that had no copy. This repo's marketplace install and rehydrate register after the boot and were already copied. Whether the cloud runtime registers HotCRM during the boot was not walked. The card's reading (18 `crm_*` and 8 `ai_*` objects missing) fits that path.
- **Finding, same defect class, not fixed here: `list_actions` / `run_action`.** `collectActionDeclarations` reads `metadata.listObjects()`, and action resolution reads the same service. Measured on the same `env_local` during-boot fixture: an object action declared `operation: 'update'` with `ai: { exposed: true }` is in the registry, but `list_actions` answers `[]` and `run_action` answers `Action 'mark_done' not found on object 'qa_pkg_open'`. Control without an `environmentId`: listed and resolved. Left for the seat to file. It touches the action resolution path, which is not a mechanical swap.
- **Finding, the stdio half (`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`):** the same three answers, measured above. Held off by the dispatch.
- **Note:** the `GATED_ACTIONS` docblock in `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts` says the HTTP bridge answers `listObjects` / `describeObject` "straight off the metadata service". After this change, it reads the protocol's merged listing. The parity claim it makes (those two are not gated through `callData`) still holds. Only the wording is stale.
